content: Saint Paul Hospital is a comprehensive medical complex located in the central area of Hanoi, the capital city of Vietnam. The hospital was originally established during the French colonial period in Indochina, which spanned the late 19th and early 20th centuries. In 2001, the hospital received significant support from several United States-based non-governmental organizations, including Counterpart International, Project HOPE, and World Medical Relief. These organizations provided medicines and medical equipment valued at USD 302,457 to enhance the hospital's emergency services. In January 2007, Norway, the United States, Japan, and the Netherlands collectively pledged a donation of 7 million US dollars to fund the establishment of a state-of-the-art research center at the hospital. According to the plans announced by the Hanoi Health Department, Saint Paul Hospital is set to undergo substantial upgrades. These include the construction of a six-story building with 100 beds dedicated to the Therapeutics Ward and another similar building with 150 beds for the Pediatrics Ward. Additionally, after renovations, the hospital's second branch will be expanded to accommodate 500 beds.
